stem.en: A student wants to watch a living amoeba move, and chooses an electron microscope because it is the strongest. What is wrong with this plan?

text.en: Specimens in an electron microscope are not alive, so nothing moves.
An electron microscope cannot magnify anything as small as an amoeba.

feedback.en: It magnifies far more than is needed for an amoeba.

text.en: An amoeba is too large to be seen with any kind of microscope at all.

feedback.en: An amoeba is easily seen with a school light microscope.

text.en: An amoeba only moves when it is under visible red light from a mirror.

feedback.en: Nothing about an amoeba depends on the colour of the light.

explanation.en:
**Why "specimens are not alive" is right**

The strongest microscope is not always the right one. A specimen for an electron microscope is not alive, so to watch an amoeba move you need a light microscope.

**Why the others are not**

- **Cannot magnify enough** - it magnifies far more than this job needs.
- **Too large** - an amoeba fits well under a light microscope.
- **Needs red light** - this has no link with how an amoeba moves.

hints.en: What is the student trying to see?
Can a specimen be alive in an electron microscope?
